system_overview: This module contains an interactive formal proof of correctness for the Boyer-Moore majority vote algorithm. It extends the main algorithm specification with lemmas and a machine-checked proof that the algorithm correctly identifies the only possible majority element. The proof is structured to be verified by the TLA+ Proof System (TLAPS).
actors_and_components: The module imports the main majority vote specification and extends it with proof obligations. It uses finite set theory lemmas from a standard proof library. The proof establishes two main results: type correctness and the correctness of the algorithm's output.
state_variables: No new state variables are introduced. All state variables are inherited from the main majority vote specification.
actions: No new actions are defined. All transitions are inherited from the main specification.
safety_properties: Two properties are formally proved: (1) Type correctness is an invariant of the specification, proved by showing it holds initially and is preserved by every transition. (2) The main correctness property is an invariant: after scanning the entire sequence, any value occurring in a strict majority of positions must equal the candidate. This is proved via the inductive invariant from the main specification.
additional_assumptions: The proof relies on TLAPS (TLA+ Proof System) for machine-checked verification. It uses auxiliary lemmas about finite set cardinality and properties of occurrence counting functions (positions before a given index form finite subsets of integers, adding an element to a finite set increases cardinality by one, etc.). The proof structure is hierarchical with numbered proof steps.
